rationale: Queuing a focused probe for a distinct consequence of the same configuration gap: a node restarted with the smaller snapshot configuration should reject a vote request from a server that the configuration in force contains but its recovered set does not, which would exclude an eligible participant from quorum formation. The probe isolates the membership rule from the leader-availability rule by comparing two requests that differ only in whether the candidate is in the node's recovered set, both carrying the leadership-transfer flag so the leader check cannot reject either. Local construction feedback shows the test passing; the retained receipt is what the account will rest on.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with the smaller configuration recorded in its snapshot reject vote requests from servers that the configuration in force contains but its recovered voter set does not, so that an eligible participant cannot obtain its vote?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote's membership rejection tests the candidate against the node's recovered configuration without any notion of the configuration in force, so a server added after the node's snapshot is rejected even though it is a voter everywhere else; the same request shape from a candidate that is inside the recovered set is granted, which isolates the rejection to the membership rule.
investigations.discriminator: Restart a node from a snapshot that records a three-voter configuration while the configuration in force has five voters, then send it vote requests that differ only in the candidate identity: one from a voter in the configuration in force but outside the recovered set, and one from a voter inside the recovered set, both flagged as leadership transfers and with an up-to-date log, and compare the granted results.

scope.description: A five-peer in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled is reduced to three voters, one node snapshots in that state, the two removed voters are re-added and traffic is committed, and that node is restarted from its stores so its recovered configuration is the three-voter set. Two vote requests are then delivered over the transport from different candidates, identical except for identity and both flagged as leadership transfers.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The candidates' requests carry a higher term and an up-to-date log so that only the membership rule and, for the control, the remaining checks decide the outcome.
Both requests set the leadership-transfer flag, which the vote handler uses to skip its leader-availability rejection, so the comparison isolates the membership rule.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer the two voters that will be re-added; apply pre-snapshot commands; snapshot the node under test while the three-voter configuration is committed; AddVoter both nodes again; apply twenty traffic commands so the node's staged commit index passes those entries; capture its configuration, shut it down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire the transports; emit a setup event with the recovered and in-force voter sets and the two candidate identities, then send two RequestVote messages over the transport, one from the re-added voter (outside the recovered set) and one from a voter inside it, both with a higher term, an up-to-date log and the leadership-transfer flag set; emit the event with both results, the recovered and in-force voter sets, and whether each candidate is a member of the configuration in force.
experiment.requirement: A node must treat a server that the configuration in force lists as a voter as an eligible participant, so that elections can still gather a majority of the configuration in force.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: requestVote decides membership from the configuration the node recovered, and the recovery path is what leaves that configuration behind the log's committed history.

comparisons.description: A voter of the configuration in force that is outside the recovered set is not rejected while the control candidate inside the recovered set is granted.
